any question about matters on the agenda, or requests for assistance, please contact the Glendale
Water & Power Administration Office at (818) 548-2107 during regular business hours.

language translation, and Braille transcripts are available upon request. Assisted listening devices
are available same-day upon request. At least 48 hours (or two business days) notice is required for
requests regarding sign language translation and Braille transcription services. All documents
related to open session items on this agenda that are received less than 72 hours prior to this
meeting, and are public records, will be available for review in the Office of the City Clerk, 613 E.

MINUTES
  GLENDALE WATER & POWER COMMISSION

  CITY HALL - COUNCIL CHAMBER
  613 E. Broadway, 2nd Floor, Glendale, CA 91206

  Monday, March 6, 2023, 4:00 PM

1. ROLL CALL
  The meeting was called to order at 4:02 p.m.

  Present: President Peterson, Commissioners Fay, Jazmadarian and Lowery

2. GWP COMMISSION/STAFF COMMENTS
  Scott Mellon, Assistant General Manager - Power Management, stated that he is filling in for
  General Manager, Mark Young, due to illness.

  President Peterson Commissioner explained the protocol of the GWP Commission elections
  which took place during this meeting.

3. ACTIONS
  a. GWP Commission Elections (President and Secretary)
  Dorine Martirosian, Principal Assistant City Attorney, conveyed that General Manager Mark
  Young recommended that the elections be delayed to the next GWP Commission meeting
  on April 3, 2023 because a new GWP Commissioner will be appointed at the City Council
  meeting on March 7, 2023. Ms. Martirosian stated that if the GWP Commission would like
  to proceed with the elections, regardless, she would facilitate the election.

  President Peterson preferred to proceed with the elections and asked if the commissioners
  concurred. All were in favor of nominating a new President and Secretary. Moving forward,
  he opened the nominations for the President and Secretary positions. Commissioner Fay
  nominated Commissioner Jazmadarian for GWP Commission President, and Commissioner
  Peterson nominated Commissioner Fay for Secretary. Commissioner Jazmadarian was
  unanimously appointed as the President of the Commission, and Commissioner Fay was
  unanimously appointed as Secretary of the Commission. President Jazmadarian assumed
  the role of President for the remainder of the meeting.

4. REPORTS - INFORMATION
  a. Public Benefit Programs
  Scott Mellon, Assistant General Manager - Power Management, introduced Mr. Herbert
  García, Public Benefits Marketing Manager, to give an overview on the Public Benefit
  Programs.

  1
   Mr. García gave an overview regarding GWP’s Public Benefit Programs in Glendale.
  He provided a brief background about the Public Benefits Programs, state law requirements
  and the four categories in which funds must be used (e.g., cost-effective energy efficiency
  and conservation, new investments in renewable energy resources, research, development
  and demonstration, and low-income electricity customers). He also discussed California
  Public Utilities Commission (CPUC) regulations and Low-Income Programs for qualifying
  families, and Energy Efficiency.

  Mr. García provided information on each of GWP’s Public Benefits Programs with
  emphasis on the programs that prove to be extremely beneficial to low-income residents,
  and residents having difficulties paying their utility bill (Helping Hand and Guardian
  Programs). He highlighted programs in reference to Smart Home Energy and Water
  Saving Upgrades; Smart Home Rebates Programs; Business Energy Solutions; GWP’s
  Online Store for Energy and Water Efficiency Measures (residents can purchase energy
  and water saving devices for home usage), and the Tree Power Program (qualifying
  customers receive up to three shade trees, stakes, ties and arbor guards at no cost); Solar
  Solutions, and In School Energy and Water Conservation Education (this program educates
  sixth grade science students in areas of energy and water conservation through a “hands
  on” curriculum). One aspect of the Solar Program has been the partnering of GWP with
  local public schools to educate kids (K-12) and teachers about solar energy and training.

  Mr. García discussed the Peak Time of Use Energy Monitor (this program has not been
  launched yet; however, the goal is to have it ready before the end of this fiscal year);
  Laundry to Landscape DIY Greywater Systems; Smart Home Display/Thermostat (this is
  an “in home display” that acts as home area network to access real time electric and
  next day water consumption), an Energy Efficiency Comparison and Potential Forecast.

  Mr. García and Mr. Craig Kuennen, Assistant General Manager - Business Services,
  addressed questions by the Commissioners regarding this report, including but not limited
  to the establishment of the current percent charge (3.6%) of retail electric revenues towards
  Public Benefits Programs; GWP’s focus on peak period programs; smart home rebates
  and home energy audits and potential similar programs such as HVAC rebates. Further
  discussion was held on questions relating to the percentage of public benefits funds
  dispersed on an annual basis; the most popular programs; Smart Home Display Thermostat
  and its functions; the Guardian Program (life-saving medical equipment); and energy
  efficiency forecast, and the consideration of factors for research and development from
  a municipal utility perspective in terms of funds being used for PBC programs.

  Commissioner Lowery commended GWP’s Tree Power Program and his positive
  experience in participating in the program.

b. Energy Briefing
  Scott Mellon, Assistant General Manager - Power Management, provided an energy
  briefing on GWP’s clean energy initiatives.

  Mr. Mellon provided the status of the Renewables Portfolio Standard and GWP’s
  Power Content Label, and Distributed Energy Sources. He provided an update regarding
  Solar on City-owned sites and the upcoming RFP to engineer, procure and construct
  solar on eight City sites; Glendale’s comparison with other cities in terms of percentage
  of customers with PV capacity in which Glendale is doing quite well; Energy Efficiency
  Programs, including the Franklin Energy Demand Response (Peak Savings Program)
  and the Willdan Energy Efficiency Program (Business Energy Upgrade).

  2
   Mr. Mellon also discussed Transportation Electrification, and City-Owned EV Charging
  Infrastructure (GWP recently had a EV Ribbon Cutting Ceremony on February 22nd for 25
  newly installed EV chargers at the Glendale Marketplace Parking Structure); Off-Peak EV
  Charging Rebate Program (GWP encourages EV drivers to participate in the rebate
  program); He provided an update on the Grayson Repower Project (an award
  recommendation will be made to Council on March 21st); the Scholl Canyon LFG; 2024
  Integrated Resource Plan (bids were just received, and the final IRP draft is scheduled for
  October 2023), and outlined the Energy Supply Challenges and Opportunities for several
  projects such as the Grayson Repower Replacement Energy.

  Mr. Mellon, Ms. Chie Valdez, Integrated Resource Planning Administrator, and
  additional GWP staff members (Craig Kuennen, Daniel Scorza, Herbert Garcia and
  Aneta Badalian) responded to the Commissioners’ questions regarding the report

5. ORAL COMMUNICATIONS
  Alexander Yessayantz

6. AGENDA FORECAST
  The Commissioners reviewed the agenda forecast for the April 3, 2023 Commission Meeting.
  Mr. Mellon noted that the Agenda Forecast may change depending on the directive of General
  Manager Mark Young. The following topics were discussed as possible future agenda items:

  •  President Jazmadarian - incentive programs and turnaround time; project benchmarking;
  turnaround time when applying for permits; water supplies; snowpack and what we can
  expect this year due to all the snow and rain; water conservation and where we go from
  here.

  •  Commissioner Fay - discussion of the process for evaluating changes to the electric rate
  structure and bonding requirements; timing of reports and recommendations relating to
  decisions regarding changes to the electric rates.

  Mr. Craig Kuennen, Assistant General Manager - Business Services, stated that the earliest
  possible meeting to present the cost of service analysis (COSA) results for electric rates is
  May 1, 2023 Commission meeting (not actually confirmed).

7. ADJOURNMENT
  Motion to Adjourn:
  Moved by: Commissioner Peterson
  Seconded by: Commissioner Fay
  Motion passed unanimously.

  Meeting was adjourned at 6:30 p.m.
